ideas.title: CPOTA: Sending Cat Photos Over HF Radio Is a Real Thing
ideas.why_now: Cat Pix on the Air ran August 8 for International Cat Day, with multiple operators making their first SSTV contact around it.
ideas.angle: Walk through how SSTV works, how CPOTA is a perfect low-stakes first attempt, and why quirky themed events like this are actually great for getting newcomers on a new mode.

ideas.title: SSTV: The Slow Picture Mode Worth Learning Right Now
ideas.why_now: SSTV spiked in activity this week thanks to CPOTA, and several ops noted it was their first time ever transmitting the mode.
ideas.angle: Cover what SSTV actually is, what software to use on Windows and Linux, and how to get your first image out without blowing it. Practical start-to-finish for the everyday ham.

ideas.title: Solar Storm Ruined Your POTA Day. Now What?

ideas.angle: Talk through practical backup plans when propagation tanks: switching bands, trying SSTV or digital modes, or just calling it and going home without shame. Normalize the pivot.

ideas.title: Your First SOTA: How It Differs From POTA and Why You Should Try It
ideas.why_now: Multiple operators logged their first SOTA activations this week, often pairing them with POTA, and the contrast between the two programs is generating fresh chatter.
ideas.angle: For the POTA crowd who has never hiked to a summit with a radio, break down what makes SOTA different: the point system, the four-contact minimum, the physical commitment, and why it is worth it.

ideas.title: Wavelog 3.1 Just Dropped: A Free Logging Tool Worth a Serious Look
ideas.why_now: Wavelog 3.1 released this week with a new Activation Planner that maps POTA, SOTA, and WWFF refs directly from your grid, plus satellite passes.
ideas.angle: Do a practical walkthrough of the new Activation Planner feature for the portable operator. Show how it changes pre-trip planning compared to juggling multiple websites.

ideas.title: LoRa Is Proprietary. Does That Put Meshtastic at Risk?
ideas.why_now: A Mastodon thread this week raised the question directly and tagged Meshtastic, MeshCore, and Reticulum, sparking real debate about the long-term foundation of mesh comms.
ideas.angle: Explain what LoRa being proprietary actually means for everyday Meshtastic users, whether open alternatives exist yet, and how much this should factor into your off-grid comms planning.

ideas.title: Passing Your General: What to Actually Do the Week After
ideas.why_now: A new General class pass post this week drew 17 comments of advice, showing strong community appetite for practical next-step guidance.
ideas.angle: Skip the vague encouragement and give a concrete first week: pick a band, find a frequency, make one SSB contact, and explore one new thing like FT8 or a net. Real steps, not a list of gear to buy.
